posts.title: Biscuit was back on his morning walk by spring
posts.excerpt: Biscuit, a beagle aged 7, was back to full walks 10 weeks after a cruciate ligament repair at Aoba Veterinary Clinic in Fairhaven.
posts.content:
10 weeks

from surgery to full walks

Biscuit is a beagle aged 7. His owner in Fairhaven was used to a morning walk that started the day. When Biscuit stopped using a hind leg as he always had, they came to Aoba Veterinary Clinic at 214 Alder Street. The clinic has been here since 2014, a general practice for dogs and cats, with surgery and dentistry in the same building. A first consultation is 30 minutes, so the opening conversation has room for a full examination rather than a glance between other tasks.

On that visit we watched how Biscuit stood and moved, and we listened to when the limp began. Cruciate ligament repair at the clinic is done by Dr. Samuel Osei, whose field is surgery and orthopaedics. He explained what the examination showed and what a repair would involve for this dog. Before any treatment, the owner received a written estimate. It covered the surgery, the anaesthetic and the monitoring, the pain relief, and the rehabilitation afterwards. The published fee list has eight lines and the prices include tax. A cruciate repair is not one of those lines, because the work depends on the dog. The figure Biscuit’s owner agreed was the figure written for him.

He came in on the day of surgery having followed the fasting times set for him. Fasting is agreed when the procedure is booked. We say when food should stop, and whether water is still appropriate, for that animal on that day. A nurse settled him. Dr. Osei carried out the repair, and a nurse stayed with the anaesthetic, watching heart rate, breathing and temperature. Biscuit then rested on a soft blanket in a recovery kennel until he was fit to travel. We told his owner how the anaesthetic had gone when he was discharged, and he went home with the notes and the pain relief already named on the estimate.

Those notes covered rest, the medicines prescribed for him, and what to watch for through the first night. A nurse called to ask how the first hours at home had been. After a visit, a nurse calls within 48 hours, and after surgery the nursing team remains the place for questions while healing is underway. Hannah Lindqvist, head veterinary nurse, leads that team. The phone, in opening hours, is +1 555 0142 300.

Rehabilitation sat with Malik Haddad, a veterinary nurse whose work is rehabilitation. His plan for Biscuit was specific to that beagle: short, calm sessions at home, real rest between them, and a pace set by how the repair felt, not by how keen Biscuit was to get through the door. The owner kept to the plan on the days when a beagle’s hope ran ahead of the leg. Every animal is different, so no date was promised at the start. This account is only what happened for Biscuit.

Ten weeks after the surgery he was back to full walks. By spring his owner said the sentence we keep with his story: “He was back on his morning walk by spring.” Those 10 weeks are his. Another dog with a cruciate injury may need a different operation, or a longer and quieter return to walking. We tell the story so the shape of one plan is visible, from the written estimate to Malik’s rehab, without turning one beagle into a forecast.

The other two records on our stories page are just as particular. Juniper, a cat aged 12, came with weight loss. Dr. Priya Nair found a thyroid condition and manages it with daily medication and checks every 3 months. Otto, a Labrador aged 8 months, had swallowed a sock. Dr. Tomás Ribeiro removed it by endoscopy, and Otto went home the same evening. None of the three is a template. They are the animals we saw, the clinicians who treated them, and the results those animals actually had.

If a limp lasts beyond 24 hours, or you are unsure whether a problem can wait, call us. A nurse will tell you whether it can wait. Urgent same-day slots are held each weekday. Out of hours, contact the regional emergency hospital. We are open Monday to Friday, 9:00–12:30 and 15:30–19:00, and Saturday, 9:00–12:30 and 15:30–17:00. Sunday and public holidays the clinic is closed. A visit can also be requested by email at hello@aobavet.example. Clara Moreau, reception and care coordinator, will help you find a time in the book.

posts.title: Juniper and the quiet thyroid
posts.excerpt: Juniper, a cat aged 12, is treated by Dr. Priya Nair for a thyroid condition with daily medication and checks every 3 months.
posts.content:
Every 3 months

thyroid checks, with daily medication

Juniper, a cat aged 12, is treated by Dr. Priya Nair for a thyroid condition with daily medication and checks every 3 months.

Weight loss and a thyroid condition

Juniper is a cat aged 12. She was brought to Aoba Veterinary Clinic because of weight loss. Dr. Priya Nair, whose field is feline medicine, examined her and diagnosed a thyroid condition. The visit followed the clinic’s usual shape. Juniper arrived in a carrier, waited in the cat room, away from dogs, and was examined with low-stress handling. The findings were explained to her owner in the room. Daily medication was recommended, and it was written down before it started. Weight loss in an older cat has more than one cause, which is why the examination and the blood work come before anyone talks about food alone. A senior blood panel, when it is the test we advise, is $110. Juniper’s plan was built for her. Every animal is different, and another cat with a changing appetite needs their own consultation.

Medication and checks every 3 months

Juniper’s thyroid condition is managed with daily medication and with checks every 3 months. Each check is a booked visit, kept to the appointment length, in the cat waiting room where pheromone diffusers are used. Her owner knows the date of the next one. Dr. Nair sees her on that schedule so the same person is comparing this visit with the last. A follow-up consultation is 15 minutes and $45 when that is the right length. A nurse calls within 48 hours of a visit if there is something new to watch. Between checks, the daily medication is the owner’s job at home, as it was written. If your cat is losing weight, drinking much more than usual, or hiding more than usual, book a 30-minute first consultation for $65. Call +1 555 0142 300 or email hello@aobavet.example.

posts.title: Otto and the sock
posts.excerpt: Otto, a Labrador aged 8 months, had a swallowed sock removed by endoscopy with Dr. Tomás Ribeiro and went home the same evening.
posts.content:
Same evening

home after the endoscopy

Otto, a Labrador aged 8 months, had a swallowed sock removed by endoscopy with Dr. Tomás Ribeiro and went home the same evening.

Removed by endoscopy

Otto is a Labrador aged 8 months. He swallowed a sock and was brought to Aoba Veterinary Clinic the same day. Dr. Tomás Ribeiro, whose field is dentistry and imaging, removed the sock by endoscopy. Otto did not go through an operation that opened the abdomen. The decision was made after he was examined, and the owner had a written estimate before the procedure. Fasting instructions, when a procedure allows time for them, are given for that animal. A nurse monitored the anaesthetic, watching heart rate, breathing and temperature. Imaging is part of Dr. Ribeiro’s work, and endoscopy sat with him. A sock is one foreign body in one dog. Every animal is different. Another swallowed object may need a different plan, which is why the clinic asks you to call rather than wait and see.

Home the same evening

Otto went home the same evening, with discharge notes from the nursing team. Hannah Lindqvist leads that team. A discharge call checked the first hours, and the usual follow-up call comes within 48 hours of a visit. He was an eight-month-old dog who could travel safely that night. That timing is what happened for Otto, not a timetable we offer for every foreign body. If you think your dog or cat has swallowed something, call +1 555 0142 300 before you do anything else at home. On a weekday we keep urgent same-day slots. When the clinic is closed, the regional emergency hospital is the right place. We are open Monday to Friday, 9:00–12:30 and 15:30–19:00, and Saturday, 9:00–12:30 and 15:30–17:00. The address is 214 Alder Street, Fairhaven.
